sentences.text: Aviatyrannis is a small coelurosaurian theropod dinosaur from the Late Jurassic of Portugal that is classified as either a tyrannosauroid or an ornithomimosaurian.
This small theropod had a holotype ilium measuring only ninety millimeters in length.
The ilium of Aviatyrannis is elongated and low, featuring a vertical ridge typical of tyrannosauroids above the hip joint.
Gregory S. Paul estimated the length of Aviatyrannis at 1 meter and its body mass at 4 kilograms, suggesting the holotype might be a juvenile.
The teeth of the praemaxilla in Aviatyrannis have a D-shaped cross-section.
The maxillary and dentary teeth of Aviatyrannis are elongated, recurving only near the top, and possess perpendicular denticles on both edges.
Oliver Walter Mischa Rauhut first reported tyrannosauroid material found in the Guimarota lignite coal mine near Leiria in 2000, initially referring it to Stokesosaurus.
Rauhut named and described the new genus Aviatyrannis with the type species Aviatyrannis jurassica in 2003 after concluding the material was distinct enough from Stokesosaurus.
The holotype specimen, IPFUB Gui Th 1, consists of a right ilium found in the early Kimmeridgian Alcobaça Formation approximately 155 million years ago.
In 2003, Rauhut referred two additional bones, a partial right ilium and a right ischium, to the genus Aviatyrannis.
Sixteen isolated teeth were referred to Aviatyrannis, including three from the premaxilla and thirteen from the maxilla and dentary.
Like other primitive tyrannosauroids, Aviatyrannis was a small bipedal predator.
Rauhut placed Aviatyrannis in the Tyrannosauroidea in a basal position in 2003.
The time range for Aviatyrannis is the Kimmeridgian stage, from 154.8 to 149.2 million years ago.
If classified as a tyrannosauroid, Aviatyrannis is one of the oldest known members of that group, potentially older than Proceratosaurus.
A 2023 study noted that the Aviatyrannis ilium is strikingly similar to that of the deinocheirid Tyrannomimus.
